relevant_findings: Edge work (cut lines) is naturally a LF-based workload and is driven by perimeter and openings geometry.
New construction commonly requires tape-line cut-to-tape when trim is sprayed enamel and walls are a contrasting system.
Higher sheens and hard-hide colors increase edge sensitivity (picture framing) and require higher discipline.
condition_drivers: Color/hide difficulty and required wet-edge discipline.
Whether trim is contrasting material/sheen (enamel vs wall paint).
Active construction dust and touch-ups after other trades.
quality_differences: QL-3: standard two-coat walls; LF edges modeled with basic discipline.
QL-4: increased sanding/inspection and tighter edge discipline.
QL-5: strict edge quality control; higher correction sensitivity.
failure_modes: Cut-line bleed or ragged lines if tape is applied/removed improperly.
Picture framing at edges (film build differences).
Flashing and lap marks due to uneven film or loss of wet edge.
notes_for_materials_manager: Tape-line strategy increases tape/plastic usage; freehand strategy increases brush time and brush consumption.
Hard-hide colors may increase roller usage and waste.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Model edges as LF tasks: tape apply/remove and cut-to-tape strokes.
Keep field coats as SF tasks; allow rounds for sanding/inspection per quality.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Use PaintScope: compute wall SF and edge LF (baseboard line, crown/ceiling line, openings if included).
Edge targets should be selectable: to_trim, to_ceiling, to_both.
assumptions: Numeric rates remain placeholders pending calibration.
uncertainties: Edge LF composition (trim-only vs trim+ceiling) depends on how PaintScope defines scope and sequencing.
